claims.text: Wear resistance of high-entropy-alloy coatings is primarily governed by nanocrystalline grain-boundary strengthening.
Nanocrystalline grain-boundary strengthening suppresses dislocation-mediated plastic deformation.
Nanocrystalline grain-boundary strengthening enhances coating adhesion.
Suppressing plastic deformation and enhancing adhesion reduces wear.
The as-deposited RHEA film is nanocrystalline, has an average grain size of approximately 18 nm, and was produced by DC magnetron sputtering.
Controlled thermal annealing can systematically coarsen the film while leaving its overall composition unchanged.
Wear testing is to be conducted at room temperature against an E52100 alloy-steel counterface.
The cited wear tests are dry tests whose conditions isolate mechanical effects from tribochemical effects.
The nanocrystalline film contains a high-density network of grain boundaries.
Fine-grain boundaries act as barriers to dislocation motion.
A high density of grain boundaries distributes strain during sliding.
The grain-boundary network strengthens the coating, improves adhesion, and delays plastic deformation during sliding.
Grain coarsening reduces grain-boundary area and enables dislocation-driven deformation.
The increased dislocation-driven deformation caused by grain coarsening produces greater material removal and higher friction.
Coatings with grain sizes below approximately 30 nm will have lower wear rates than coatings with grain sizes above approximately 30 nm.
Coatings with grain sizes below approximately 30 nm will have lower coefficients of friction than coatings with grain sizes above approximately 30 nm.
The approximately 18 nm as-deposited baseline has high hardness and adhesion.
The proposed mechanism should apply broadly to sputtered high-entropy-alloy coatings under dry, room-temperature sliding.
Elevated temperature or significant oxide formation may introduce additional wear mechanisms.
Failure of grain coarsening to measurably increase wear rate or friction relative to the approximately 18 nm baseline would falsify grain-boundary strengthening as the dominant wear mechanism.
